Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

May noun

classical

Cic. Att. 2.8.2: Kal. Majīs
Traupman 77

1Majus: consonantal i written j, with no macron before it (Lewis & Short Māius). The vowel before intervocalic j is short and the syllable heavy, as in major. Ruling: Consonantal i is written j.

Majus1, Maja, Majum

adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)

of May; May

Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Majae: the 1st, 7th and 15th. Ovid derives the name from majōrēs, “the elders”, one of three explanations he gives (F. 5.73, 427): partly right, since de Vaan (359, s.v. magnus) puts Majus with magnus and major.

Examples

  • mēnsis erat Majus, majōrum nōmine dictus

    it was the month of May, named after the eldersOv. F. 5.427

  • Quīntō diē mēnsis Majī.

    On the fifth of May (the modern way).Traupman 74

See also month, April, June, the Kalends.
